messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in Cisco Nexus Dashboard (v6.3.1). Feel free to copy the snippets into your preferred tool (Postman, cURL, PowerShell, etc.) or use the built‑in API Explorer in the Dashboard. --- ## 1. Locate the Endpoint in the Dashboard | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Log in to Cisco Nexus Dashboard. | | 2 | From the left‑hand navigation, click **API** → **API Explorer** (or **Developer** → **API Explorer**). | | 3 | In the **API Explorer** search bar, type **device connector** or **connector versions**. | | 4 | The endpoint you’re looking for will appear as:
**GET /api/v1/device-connector/versions** (exact path may vary – check the documentation). | | 5 | Click the endpoint to expand its details. | --- ## 2. Review the Endpoint Details | Item | What to Look For | |------|------------------| | **Method** | `GET` | | **Path** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Query Parameters** | None (unless the docs specify optional filters) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Response** | JSON array of connector version objects (see schema below). | --- ## 3. Generate the Request ### 3.1 Using the Built‑In “Generate Request” Button 1. With the endpoint expanded, click the **Generate Request** button (usually located at the top right of the endpoint pane). 2. A modal will pop up showing the full HTTP request (method, URL, headers, body). 3. Copy the request text or click **Copy to Clipboard**. ### 3.2 Using the “Try it Out” Feature 1. Click **Try it Out**. 2. If the endpoint requires authentication, the Dashboard will prompt you to log in or provide a token. 3. Click **Execute**. 4. The response will appear in the panel below. 5. You can click **Copy Request** or **Copy Response** to reuse the data. --- ## 4. Example Requests Below are ready‑to‑use examples for common tools. ### 4.1 cURL ```bash curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### 4.2 Postman | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | **Method** | GET | | **URL** | `https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Body** | None | ### 4.3 PowerShell (Invoke-RestMethod) ```powershell $uri = "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer " Accept = "application/json" } $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $headers -Method Get $response ``` --- ## 5. Authentication Options | Method | How to Obtain | Where to Put | |--------|---------------|--------------| | **OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token** | Use the Dashboard’s OAuth flow or obtain via the **Identity & Access Management** section. | Header: `Authorization: Bearer ` | | **Basic Auth** | Username/password or client credentials. | Header: `Authorization: Basic ` | | **API Key** | Generated under **API Keys**. | Header: `X-API-Key: ` | > **Tip:** For quick testing, the Dashboard’s **API Explorer** automatically injects a valid token when you click **Try it Out**. --- ## 6. Sample Response Schema ```json [ { "id": "12345", "name": "Connector v1.0", "status": "active", "created_at": "2024-01-15T12:34:56Z", "updated_at": "2024-02-20T08:21:30Z", "metadata": { "manufacturer": "Cisco", "model": "NX-1000", "firmware_version": "5.2.1" } }, { "id": "67890", "name": "Connector v2.0", "status": "deprecated", "created_at": "2023-11-01T09:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2024-01-10T14:15:00Z", "metadata": { "manufacturer": "Cisco", "model": "NX-2000", "firmware_version": "6.0.0" } } ] ``` > **Note:** The actual fields may differ; refer to the API documentation for the exact schema. --- ## 7. Troubleshooting | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Token expired or missing | Refresh token or re‑authenticate | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong URL or endpoint not enabled | Verify the path in the docs | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Backend issue | Check Dashboard logs or contact support | | **Rate Limit Exceeded** | Too many requests | Add `Retry-After` header or back‑off logic | --- ## 8. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Item | Example | |------|---------| | **Base URL** | `https://` | | **Endpoint** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Full URL** | `https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Method** | GET | | **cURL** | `curl -X GET "" -H "Authorization: Bearer " -H "Accept: application/json"` | | **Postman** | Set method to GET, URL to ``, add headers as above. | --- ### Final Checklist - [ ] Logged into Cisco Nexus Dashboard. - [ ] Located the **GET /api/v1/device-connector/versions** endpoint. - [ ] Generated the request using **Generate Request** or **Try it Out**. - [ ] Copied the request into your tool of choice. - [ ] Added a valid **Authorization** header. - [ ] Executed the request and verified the JSON response. Happy API testing! If you run into any specific errors, let me know the error message and I’ll help troubleshoot further.
